learningObjective: See that when a thin ring is cut and unrolled, it becomes a rectangle with width equal to the circumference (2πr) and height equal to the ring thickness — and that these rectangles stack into a triangular shape
ahaMoment: Discovering that as rings get thinner (higher ring count), the stacked rectangles form a cleaner and cleaner triangle shape, with the widest rectangle at the top (outer circumference) and shortest at the bottom (inner rings)

miniSpec.title: Ring Unwrapping Slider with Side-by-Side Views
miniSpec.manipulated_variable: A slider control that changes the number of rings the circle is divided into (from perhaps 3 to 50 rings)
miniSpec.primary_visual_feedback: The circle re-divides into more or fewer concentric rings, and simultaneously the stack of rectangles on the right updates to show correspondingly thinner or thicker rectangles, maintaining visual correspondence through color; the stacked rectangles form a stepped approximation to a triangle
miniSpec.goal_structure: Free exploration with implicit guidance toward increasing ring count to observe rectangles becoming more uniform in width and the triangle shape becoming cleaner
miniSpec.causal_chain_exposed: Each ring displays its radius value r, the corresponding rectangle shows its width labeled as 2πr, and its height labeled as dr; total area of rectangles displayed numerically approaching πr²
miniSpec.trace_strategy: None - the current state is sufficient because the concept focuses on the geometric transformation at the current subdivision level
miniSpec.aha_moment: Discovering that as rings get thinner (higher ring count), the stacked rectangles form a cleaner and cleaner triangle shape, with the widest rectangle at the top (outer circumference) and shortest at the bottom (inner rings)

modelVariables.numRings: Number of rings the circle is divided into (3-50), student-controlled
modelVariables.R: Circle radius, carried over from previous section, frozen/locked
modelVariables.unwrapping_dr: Derived: thickness of each ring = R / numRings
modelVariables.unwrapping_totalArea: Derived: sum of all rectangle areas, approaching πR²
modelVariables.unwrapping_outerCircumference: Derived: 2πR, width of the outermost rectangle

assertions.description: On load, the circle is divided into a small number of rings (5), showing visible approximation steps in the triangle
assertions.visualCheck: Circle shows 5 distinct concentric rings; right side shows 5 rectangles in a stepped staircase

assertions.description: The numRings slider can be operated
assertions.visualCheck: Circle now shows 20 thinner rings; rectangles are thinner and more numerous

assertions.description: Increasing rings makes each ring thinner (dr = R/n)
assertions.visualCheck: Ring thickness visibly decreases as ring count doubles

assertions.description: Total area of rectangles approximates πR² (the aha setup)
assertions.visualCheck: Total area readout shows value close to πR² ≈ 50.27

assertions.description: The circle radius R is carried over and cannot be changed
assertions.visualCheck: Radius shown as a fixed/locked value, not interactive

invariants.description: Ring thickness always equals R divided by number of rings
Total area of rectangles = sum of 2πr_i × dr for all rings
